newsitem.title: FRANCE: French mobile phone market grew 6.3 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: French mobile phone market grew 6.3 pct in May.

text.p: The number of subscribers to mobile phone services in France grew by 6.3 percent in May to 3.27 million, the telecommunications authority ART said in a monthly report on the sector published on Wednesday.
The digital mobile phone market grew 6.9 percent in May to 3,097,000 subscribers, while the number of clients for analogue services fell 3.6 percent to 175,500.
Bouygues Telecom, a unit of Bouygues, showed the sharpest rise in the overall market, adding 22,300 subscribers or 15.2 percent in May for a total of 169,300 subscribers.
Bouygues Telecom, the most recent of the three major players in the GSM digital mobile phone market, has added 97,200 subscribers, a rise of 135 percent, in the last six months, the report said.
France Telecom's Itineris saw growth of 6.5 percent in its subscriber base in May, giving it a total of 1.75 million subscribers.
The other main GSM player, Compagnie Generale des Eaux's SFR, also increased its subscriber base 6.5 percent in May, taking its total to 1.13 million.
Paging services, where the main operators are offshoots of the major GSM operators, saw a 6.1 percent rise in users in May to give a total of 1.38 million, ART said.
SFR's Tam-Tam and Bouygues Telecom's Kobby together represented 25 percent of the market's growth in May, helped by an end to the shortage of terminals that had hampered their growth, it said.
